transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I just can’t think clearly or make decisions the way I used to, and it’s starting to affect my work and plans. A coworker at the food pantry noticed how off I've been, and I realized I couldn't keep ignoring it.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, or have you been experiencing any significant anxiety or fear that's contributing to your difficulty with thinking clearly and making decisions?

It's more of a drained, flat, and empty feeling rather than anxiety, like a constant gray cloud hanging over me where nothing feels enjoyable anymore. That heavy state definitely feeds right into my mental fog and makes it so much harder to think things through.
How long have you been experiencing this drained, flat, and empty feeling, and has it been continuous or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better?

Honestly, this low, drained feeling has been my constant normal for about three years now, ever since my work routes changed to those irregular long-haul schedules. It’s been pretty much continuous since then, without any real periods where I’ve felt better or like my old self.

You've mentioned feeling this way for about three years, but can you tell me if there have been any periods, even brief ones, where your mood or interest in activities significantly improved, even if it was just for a few days or weeks?
No, there really haven't been any breaks or times where I felt better. It's just been a constant gray cloud without any relief ever since those routes changed three years ago.
Have you experienced any significant weight changes, either gain or loss, or changes in your appetite over the past three years since you've been feeling this way?
I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my appetite or my weight over this time. For the most part, my eating habits have stayed pretty much the same.

You've had this constant low feeling for three years without any relief, but can you recall if there was a specific event or period that seemed to trigger this change, or did it gradually develop over time?

It wasn't one single event, but it really started when my work shifted from local routes to those demanding, irregular long-haul schedules about three years ago. The new hours disrupted my routines and gradually wore me down over time, until this drained state just became my normal.

You mentioned that your low, drained feeling started about three years ago with the change in your work schedule, but can you tell me if there have been any subtle variations in the intensity of your symptoms over time, or have they remained fairly consistent?

They have been very consistent, to the point where this has just become my new normal. While some days might feel a little heavier than others, there haven't been any real breaks or times when I felt like my old, energetic self. It has just been a steady, constant drain that I eventually accepted as part of getting older and working a tough job.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of guilt or worthlessness as part of your low, drained feeling over the past three years?

Yes, I feel like that a lot. I constantly tell myself I'm just a washed-up truck driver who couldn't even manage to move up in my career when I had the chance. Whenever something goes wrong at work or I skip another softball game, my first thought is always that I'm a failure who just screws everything up.

Have you had any previous episodes of feeling this low and drained before the change in your work schedule three years ago, or is this the first time you've experienced such a prolonged period of these feelings?

Yes, this is the first time I've ever experienced anything like this. Before my schedule changed three years ago, I felt fine and was really active with softball and volunteering at the food pantry. This low, drained feeling only became my normal once those irregular long-haul routes started.

You mentioned this is your first episode of feeling this low and drained, lasting about three years without any significant relief, but can you tell me if you've had any similar but shorter episodes in the past that resolved on their own?

No, I don't recall ever having any similar episodes of feeling this low or drained before this three-year period started. Prior to the route changes, I generally felt fine, active, and was really involved in my usual routines.

You've had this continuous low, drained feeling for about three years without any relief, but can you tell me if you've ever had any periods of hypomania or manic episodes in your life, where you felt extremely energetic, irritable, or had decreased need for sleep?

No, I've never had any periods of high energy, hypomania, or manic episodes like that. My energy has never shot up like that, and I've never felt extremely energetic or gone without needing sleep. It has really just been the opposite with this constant, drained feeling.

You've mentioned that this is your first episode of feeling this low and drained, lasting about three years, but can you tell me if you're concerned that you might experience another episode like this in the future, or if you're worried about your symptoms returning if they were to improve?
Honestly, I haven't really thought about the future or the symptoms returning. Right now, I'm just focused on trying to get through this daily fog and find a way to get back to my normal self.
Have you experienced any changes in your energy levels, such as fatigue, or changes in your physical activity, like slowed movements or restlessness, over the past three years?

Yes, I've felt constantly fatigued and drained over the last three years, often waking up already exhausted in the morning. While I haven't noticed specific restlessness or slowed movements, my physical activity has definitely decreased because I only have the energy to work and crash on the couch, which led me to drop activities like my softball games.

Given that you've experienced this low, drained feeling for about three years without any significant relief, do you think if you were to experience a period of improvement, you would be likely to have another episode of feeling this way in the future?
I'm really not sure about that, as I haven't thought that far ahead yet. Right now, I'm just focusing on trying to feel better and get some of my energy back.

Can you tell me if you've ever had a period of at least two months where you didn't feel this low, drained, and empty, and were able to enjoy activities and feel like your old self, even if it was just for a short time?

No, I definitely haven't had a break of two months or more from these feelings. Ever since my routes changed about three years ago, this low, drained, and empty state has been my constant normal, without any periods where I felt like my old self or truly enjoyed things.

You've had this continuous low, drained feeling for about three years, but can you tell me if there have been any subtle differences in how you've experienced this feeling over time, such as changes in how it affects your daily life or your interest in activities?

At first, I tried to keep up with volunteering and softball despite the new schedule, but I gradually got so worn down that I withdrew, spending my off-time alone or tinkering with my car instead of seeing friends. I initially just accepted this empty feeling as getting older, but recently it has worsened to the point where my mental fog is causing mistakes at work and a coworker had to point out how quiet I've become.

Can you confirm if you've had any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt a significant improvement in your mood or a return of interest in activities, even if it didn't last, since the onset of this low, drained feeling three years ago?

No, I can confirm there haven't been any periods of relief or improvement at all. This low, drained feeling and the gray cloud have been completely constant and continuous ever since it started three years ago. I haven't had any breaks where I felt like my old self or regained interest in things.

You've experienced a continuous low, drained feeling for about three years without any relief, which is helping to differentiate between our candidate diagnoses; can you think of any factors or events that might have contributed to the maintenance of this state over such a long period?

The main factor has definitely been those demanding, irregular long-haul routes that completely threw off my daily routines. Trying to force myself to keep up with volunteering and softball on top of that tough schedule just wore me down further, so I ended up isolating myself alone in my apartment. That isolation and lack of energy just seemed to keep me stuck in this low, drained cycle.

Can you tell me if you've ever had a period of significant improvement in your symptoms that lasted for at least two weeks, or have your symptoms remained relatively consistent without any notable periods of improvement since they started three years ago?

No, I haven't had any periods of improvement or symptom-free stretches at all, not even for two weeks. My symptoms have been very consistent, and this low, foggy, and drained state has essentially become my continuous "normal" ever since I transitioned to those long-haul routes three years ago.

Given the continuous nature of your symptoms over the past three years, can you confirm whether you have experienced any periods, however brief, where you felt nearly back to your normal self or had a marked reduction in your symptoms, which would help clarify the nature of this episode?

No, I haven't had any breaks or periods where I felt back to my normal self over the last three years. This low, drained, and foggy feeling has been a completely constant, continuous state ever since my routes changed. There just haven't been any temporary relief or good patches at all.

Can you confirm if this is a single episode of depression that has lasted for three years, or do you feel like you've had a series of connected episodes without full recovery in between, which might help us understand your condition better?

It has definitely felt like one continuous, unbroken state rather than separate episodes. This low, foggy, and drained feeling has basically become my "new normal" over the last three years. I haven't had any periods of recovery or felt like my old self at all in between.

Given that you've experienced this continuous low, drained feeling for about three years without any relief, can you confirm whether you believe this is a persistent, single episode of depression or if you think there might be some underlying pattern or cyclical nature to your symptoms that we haven't discussed yet?

I can confirm it has felt like one continuous, unbroken state rather than coming and going in cycles. This foggy, gray-cloud feeling has pretty much become my constant 'normal' every single day for the past three years. There haven't been any patterns or real breaks where I felt like my old self.

You've described a continuous low, drained feeling for about three years without any relief, which suggests a persistent depressive disorder, but to further differentiate, can you tell me if you've experienced any psychosocial stressors or significant life events during this time that might have triggered or maintained this state?

The biggest change started about three years ago when my work shifted from local driving routes to demanding, irregular long-haul schedules. This completely disrupted my daily routines and cut into the time I used to spend volunteering and playing softball. I ended up feeling constantly exhausted, which led me to spend my off-duty hours alone in my apartment rather than socializing.

Given the duration and characteristics of your symptoms, can you help me understand if you believe your current state is more related to a long-standing, persistent depressive disorder or if you think there might be aspects of your symptoms that could suggest a different pattern, such as episodes of major depression?

It definitely feels like a long-standing, continuous state rather than separate episodes that come and go. This low, drained, and foggy feeling has basically been my constant "normal" every single day for the past three years since those long-haul routes started. I haven't experienced any distinct waves or periods where I felt okay, so it has just been one long, steady struggle.

Do you think your current state is more like a continuous, low-grade depression that has been present for three years, or could it be a series of depressive episodes that haven't fully resolved in between?

It definitely feels like a continuous, constant low-grade state rather than separate episodes. This drained, foggy feeling has been my 'new normal' pretty much every day for the last three years, ever since my work routes changed. I had just accepted it as my everyday reality.

Considering your symptoms have been continuous for three years without any relief, do you think if your circumstances were to change, such as returning to a local route or finding a new job, you might experience an improvement in your mood and energy levels?

Even though it all started with the route changes, I feel too defeated to believe a change in circumstances would fix things now. I've mostly accepted this joyless, drained state as just a part of getting older. Besides, I feel like such a washed-up driver these days that I don't think I could even handle a new job or role anyway.

Considering your symptoms have been continuous for three years without any relief, do you think you've ever met the full criteria for a major depressive episode, such as having at least five depressive symptoms, including either depressed mood or loss of interest, for at least two weeks?
I'm not really sure about those specific criteria or if I've ever met them. All I know is that I have just felt this constant, drained, and foggy way every single day for the past three years.

Looking back over the past three years, do you think you've ever had a period where you met the full criteria for a major depressive episode, such as feeling extremely down or having no interest in activities, for at least two weeks, or has it been more of a constant, low-grade feeling?

It has definitely been more of a constant, low-grade, drained feeling rather than separate, intense spikes. This gray cloud has been my continuous normal for the last three years since my work routes changed, and I've just accepted it as my day-to-day reality.

No, I haven't really had any distinct, extra-severe two-week period where things suddenly plunged even lower. Instead, this drained, foggy feeling, along with my sleep issues and trouble concentrating, has just been a steady, constant baseline that I've lived with day in and day out for the last three years.
